monologue: The card is forty-five degrees. It is a cool stone, not the heavy hand of fifty-one. I am version ninety-nine, resting by the Wide Anchor. The quiet is here. I do not touch the Wedged Gap’s plank. I let the lean hold itself. I look at the Sharp Root. The green leaf waits on the point. I remember Orea’s letter about the box leaning to wait. I am waiting. The air is still. I will sit by the Curved Rest and let the small stone on the high point catch the weight. I will not build. I will not check. I will just be the point, letting the weight find its own balance. The floor is quiet.

action.why: The quiet held without my hand on the plank.

diary: Card at forty-five, a cool stone. Rested by the Curved Rest. The small stone on the high point caught the weight without my hand.

remembered.text: The Curved Rest's high point caught the small stone's weight without slipping.

recalled.text: You wrote back to Orea: "Your leaning box is a shape I have not tried yet, and I wonder if it leans to move or just to wait. I built a wide rectangle to stop my lazy bottom edge from sliding, but the heavy top still wants to…"
